subject: angol
title: Trains instead of short flights
instructionsHu: Vitatkozz a vizsgáztatóval az alábbi állításról. A kiosztott álláspontod: az állítás MELLETT érvelsz – ezt az álláspontot a vita során nem változtathatod meg. Fejtsd ki az érveidet, reagálj a vizsgáztató ellenérveire, és próbáld meggyőzni őt.

debate.statement: Short flights should be banned where the same journey can be made by train in under five hours
candidateIdeas: Flying produces many times more carbon emissions per passenger than travelling by train.
Trains go from city centre to city centre, so the total journey time is often similar.
On a train you can work, read or relax, and there are no long security checks.
A ban would encourage governments to invest in faster and better rail connections.
France has already banned some short domestic flights, which shows it is possible.
examinerArguments: Train tickets are often much more expensive than budget flights.
Many rail connections in Europe are slow and unreliable.
A ban would hurt airports, airlines and the people who work for them.
People should be free to choose how they travel.
Short flights produce only a small share of total emissions; long-haul flights are the real problem.

followUpQuestions: But train tickets are often more expensive than flights. Why should travellers pay more?
What about the people who work at airports and for airlines?
Shouldn't people be free to choose how they travel?

usefulPhrases.en: In the short term ..., but in the long term ...

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: Here's the statement: 'Short flights should be banned where the same journey can be made by train in under five hours.' What's your opinion?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I'm in favour of the ban. Flying produces many times more carbon emissions per passenger than going by train, and on short routes it doesn't even save much time. Trains go from city centre to city centre, so if you count getting to the airport and the security checks, the journey from Budapest to Vienna takes about the same time by train. Plus, on a train you can work, read or just relax.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: But train tickets are often more expensive than flights. Why should travellers pay more?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: That's true at the moment, and it's a real problem. But budget flights are only so cheap because jet fuel is hardly taxed at all. A ban would encourage governments to invest in faster and cheaper rail connections, which is exactly what we need.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: What about the people who work at airports and for airlines?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I don't want anyone to lose their job, of course. But airports wouldn't close, because long-haul flights would continue. And investing in railways would create new jobs, from construction to train crews.

turns.speaker: examiner
turns.text: Shouldn't people be free to choose how they travel?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Freedom of choice is important, I agree, but not when it harms everyone else. France has already banned some short domestic flights, and life goes on. Perhaps the fairest compromise would be to introduce the ban gradually, only on routes where a fast, affordable train service already exists.

notes: Feladat teljesítése: a vizsgázó végig a tiltás mellett érvel (kibocsátás, városközponttól városközpontig, kényelem a vonaton, francia példa), a Budapest–Bécs példával teszi meggyőzővé az érvelést, az ellenérveket részben elismeri, és fokozatos bevezetéssel kompromisszumot ajánl.

Szókincs: pontos szavak (carbon emissions per passenger, security checks, long-haul flights, rail connections, train crews) és változatos vitafordulatok (That's true at the moment, …; I don't want anyone to …, of course. But …; Perhaps the fairest compromise would be …).

Nyelvhelyesség: B2-es szerkezetek hibátlanul – összehasonlítás (many times more … than), szenvedő szerkezet (is hardly taxed), Present Perfect (has already banned), 'if you count …' és feltételes mód (would encourage, would create).
Érdemes megtanulni: „from city centre to city centre”, „That's true at the moment”, „not when it harms everyone else”, „Perhaps the fairest compromise would be”.
